title_html: By the Time She Reaches the Pilot
title_plain: The Language of Maritime Safety -- SOLAS, Evacuation and the Future of an Operational Plan
menu_desc: Evacuation, life raft, watertight compartment and distress call, and the two futures an operational order is written in -- 35 slides
hero_line: An operational order is written in a tense most people never use. That is why it reads as if it had already happened.
grammar_point: future perfect and future continuous in operational planning

warmup.p: You wrote the same situation in both forms and said what changes on board. Read two pairs out loud and say which of the two a report would prefer.

provoke.task: Say when the round happens and when the ship arrives, in that order. Then say what the sentence would mean if it read the crew will complete the round when the vessel reaches the pilot station.

reading_sub: A company instruction, and the incident that produced it

paras: The following instruction applies to every vessel in the fleet from the first of next month. By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, her crew will have completed the pre-arrival safety round in full, and the muster list, the life jacket count and the life raft release arrangements will have been verified by name and not by signature. The deck team will be standing by fore and aft from thirty minutes before the pilot boards.

The instruction is issued because of an evacuation that did not go badly. In February a fire in a machinery space was contained by the fixed fire suppression system within four minutes, the watertight compartment was sealed, and no distress call was ever transmitted. There were no casualties and there was no salvage. On any measure the outcome was good.

What the debrief found was that almost none of it had been planned. Two of the twenty-one people on board went to the wrong muster station, because the list had not been updated since the last crew change. Four life jackets were in a locker that had been painted shut. The order to abandon ship was never given, which is the only reason those two facts cost nothing at all. Had the fire spread for another six minutes, this would be a different document.

From the first of next month, therefore, every master will be reporting the pre-arrival round by name, and by the end of the quarter the company will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet. None of this makes a ship safer by itself. What makes a ship safer is that on the next occasion, the people who go to the wrong station will be doing it in a drill.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- fleet safety instruction written for this lesson in the register of the PS-ASON reading passages

choices: Because an evacuation went badly and people were hurt.
Because an incident ended well by luck rather than by preparation, and the debrief said so.
Because the fixed fire suppression system failed to contain the fire.

grammar_question: Two of these are finished before a moment that has not arrived yet, and one is still going on at it. Sort them -- and then find the two little words the finished ones cannot do without.
grammar_rows: future perfect: complete BEFORE a stated point in the future
By the time she arrives, the crew will have completed the round.
future continuous: in progress AT that point, not finished
The deck team will be standing by fore and aft.
future perfect passive: already done by then, by somebody the text does not name
by / by the time / by the end of
the deadline the future perfect needs. Without it the tense has nothing to be earlier than
by the end of the quarter the company will have replaced...
used to / be used to / get used to
a past habit now over / being accustomed to something / becoming accustomed to it
She used to serve on tankers. She is used to working night watches.

future perfect says FINISHED BEFORE; simple future says AT or AFTER. An option that turns will have completed the round into will complete the round on arrival moves the whole operation to the wrong side of the deadline, and every other word stays the same.
grammar_insight: An operational order is written in the future perfect because it describes a state the ship has to be IN when the moment comes, not a task she starts then. Read the deadline first, then decide which side of it the verb sits on.

quickfire.situation: By the time she arrives, the crew will have completed the round. Which happens first?
tips: The round. Future perfect means finished BEFORE the stated moment.
Will complete on arrival would put it after.

quickfire.situation: The deck team will be standing by fore and aft. Is that finished or in progress at the moment described?
tips: In progress. Future continuous describes the state the ship is in at that point.
It has not ended when the pilot boards -- that is the whole point of it.

quickfire.situation: Say, in exam register, that nobody was hurt or killed.
tips: The incident exacted no human toll.

quickfire.situation: Had the fire spread for another six minutes. Rewrite that with if.
tips: If the fire had spread for another six minutes.
The inversion replaces if -- it is the same conditional, one register higher.

quickfire.situation: She used to serve on tankers. She is used to night watches. Which is a finished habit?
tips: Used to serve: a past habit that is over.
Be used to means accustomed, and is followed by a noun or -ing.

quickfire.situation: An option says: the fire was extinguished by the crew with portable equipment. Is that in the text?
tips: No. It was contained by the FIXED fire suppression system.
The option keeps the topic and changes the agent.

prod_sub: Two recordings, then the instruction in your own words

listenings.h: Four Minutes in a Machinery Space
listenings.sub: The chief engineer on the February fire. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: The fixed system did exactly what it was designed to do, and I want that on the record, because everything else I am going to say sounds like criticism. Four minutes from detection to containment, compartment sealed, no distress call, nobody hurt. If you read only the numbers it is a good day. What the numbers do not show is that two people arrived at the wrong muster station and asked me where they should be, and that when I went to check the forward locker afterwards I could not open it, because somebody had painted it shut at the last dry dock and nobody had opened it since. We were four minutes and a closed door away from a very different conversation. The order to abandon ship was never given. That is the only reason those two things are anecdotes and not findings.
questions: What does he insist on putting on the record first?
That the fixed system did exactly what it was designed to do: four minutes from detection to containment, compartment sealed, no distress call, nobody hurt.
What do the numbers not show?
That two people arrived at the wrong muster station, and that the forward locker could not be opened because it had been painted shut at the last dry dock.
Why does he say those two things are anecdotes and not findings?
Because the order to abandon ship was never given. If it had been, they would have mattered.

listenings.h: What the Instruction Will Actually Change
listenings.sub: The fleet safety manager explains the new order. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I will tell you what this instruction does and what it does not do, because I would rather say it than have it discovered. It does not make anybody safer on its own. Nothing written down does. What it changes is one word: verification is by name, not by signature. From the first of next month, by the time a ship reaches the pilot station her crew will have completed the round person by person, and the master will be reporting it that way, out loud, on the record. By the end of the quarter we will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet, which will take four months and cost less than one day of detention. And the honest measure of whether any of it worked is not the paperwork. It is whether the next two people who go to the wrong station are doing it in a drill.
questions: What does she say the instruction does not do?
It does not make anybody safer on its own. Nothing written down does.
What is the one word that changes, and what does it mean in practice?
Verification is by name and not by signature: the round is completed person by person, and the master reports it that way, out loud and on the record.
What does she give as the honest measure of success?
Not the paperwork, but whether the next two people who go to the wrong station are doing it in a drill.

roleplays.label: Guided
roleplays.scenario: Deliver the instruction in five sentences, in this order: what will be complete by the pilot station, what the deck team will be doing, why the instruction exists, what went wrong in February, and what the company will have done by the end of the quarter. Use one future form in each of the first two and the last.
chips: By the time a ship reaches the pilot station...
The deck team will be standing by...
By the end of the quarter we will have...

roleplays.label: Semi-free
roleplays.scenario: The February incident ended well and the debrief was severe. Explain out loud how both of those can be true at once, and say which of the two the company is entitled to take credit for. You may not use the word lucky.
chips: the list had not been updated
the outcome does not measure the preparation

roleplays.label: Free
roleplays.scenario: Close the text. You are the safety manager and there has just been a second incident, this time with an order to abandon ship. In about two minutes, say out loud what the new instruction will require and by when. Everything you promise has to be finished before a deadline you name.
roleplays.note: No support. Target: at least three future perfects, each with its own by-phrase, and one future continuous.

wrap_head: You Read the Deadline Before the Verb
survival: By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, her crew will have completed the pre-arrival round.
The deck team will be standing by fore and aft from thirty minutes before the pilot boards.
The fire was contained by the fixed fire suppression system within four minutes.
The order to abandon ship was never given, and no distress call was transmitted.
By the end of the quarter the company will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet.
checklist: I can tell will have done from will be doing and say which side of the deadline each one is on.
I look for the by-phrase before I decide what the future perfect is measured against.
I know the difference between used to do and be used to doing.
I can name the emergency equipment a SOLAS text assumes I know.
I can turn a good outcome into an honest debrief, out loud.
badge_line: A good outcome is not a good preparation, and now you can read the difference in the tense.

pc_desc: The vocabulary of shipboard emergency and the two futures an operational order is written in. Key words: evacuation, life jacket, life raft, fire suppression, watertight compartment, emergency signal, abandon ship, casualty, salvage, distress call. Structure: future perfect and future continuous in operational planning.

paras: By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, her crew will have completed the pre-arrival safety round, and the life raft release arrangements will have been verified by name. The deck team will be standing by fore and aft from thirty minutes before the pilot boards.

By the end of the quarter the company will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet. On the next occasion, the people who go to the wrong station will be doing it in a drill. The second officer used to serve on tankers and is used to working night watches, but it took her a full voyage to get used to the new alarm panel.

quiz.q: By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, her crew will have completed the round. Which happens first?
opts: The round is completed first; the arrival comes after it.
The ship arrives first and the round is done on arrival.
The two happen at the same moment.

quiz.q: Why will be standing by and not will stand by?
opts: Because the writer wants the action IN PROGRESS at that moment, not started then.
Because stand by has no simple future form.
Because the deck team is plural.

quiz.q: She used to serve on tankers and she is used to working night watches mean:
opts: the same thing, in two registers.
a past habit that is over, and being accustomed to something now.
a future plan, and a present obligation.

grammar_tip_title: The Two Futures of an Operational Order
grammar_tip_lead: An order describes the state a ship has to be IN when a moment arrives, not the task she starts then. That is why it is written in a tense most people never use. Find the deadline first; then decide which side of it the verb sits on.

pc_think: Close the text. In about ninety seconds, brief a crew joining next month: what has to be finished by the time the ship reaches the pilot station, what the deck team will be doing, and why the instruction exists at all. Use at least two future perfects with their own deadlines and six words from this lesson.

media.title: The 3,500-Capacity Cruise Ship Taking on Central America -- Mighty Cruise Ships (full episode)
media.desc: Three and a half thousand people, one muster list and a crew that rehearses the evacuation of a small town. Everything in today's vocabulary exists on screen, at scale.
media.tip: watch the drill sequence twice. The second time, narrate it out loud in the future perfect, as if you were writing the order the day before.

media.title: Abandon Ship Drill using Lifeboats
media.desc: The drill itself, filmed on board: muster, life jackets, boarding and lowering, in the order SOLAS requires it. The words of this lesson are the commands you will hear.
media.tip: pause at the muster and say out loud what would have to be complete BEFORE that moment for the drill to work. That is the future perfect, in its natural habitat.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): DECISAO DE DESENHO do programa: toda aula e reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (5 min): Ela escreveu oito pares de frases com os verbos da aula 7. Peca dois pares e a CONSEQUENCIA operacional de cada um. Se ela so traduzir o sentido, pergunte: and what changes on board?
teacher.s3: Provocacao (5 min): Peca a ORDEM dos dois eventos. A segunda pergunta e a que importa: 'will complete the round when the vessel reaches' poe a ronda DEPOIS da chegada -- que e o contrario do que a ordem manda. Se ela nao vir, desenhe uma linha do tempo com o dedo.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Diga: the words of an emergency, two futures, and the deadline that makes one of them possible.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words you hope never to use in order. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): evacuation, life jacket, life raft, fire suppression. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ para life raft x life boat: Is a life raft the same as a lifeboat? (Nao -- o raft e inflavel e nao tem motor; o boat e rigido. A aula 5 ja trouxe lifeboat drill.) CCQ para fire suppression: Is it a fire extinguisher? (Nao -- e a instalacao FIXA do espaco.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): watertight compartment, emergency signal, abandon ship. CCQ para abandon ship: Who can give this order? (So o comandante. E o unico item do vocabulario que e uma ORDEM, nao um objeto.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): casualty, salvage, distress call. CCQ para casualty: Does casualty mean a death? (Nao necessariamente -- morto OU ferido, e no uso formal tambem o proprio sinistro. Duplo sentido que ja caiu.) CCQ para salvage: Is salvage the same as rescue? (Nao -- salvage e o NAVIO e a CARGA; rescue sao as pessoas.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: This incident ended well, and the debrief was brutal. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Tres minutos em silencio, sem dicionario. NAO traduza. Este texto e uma ORDEM: o primeiro paragrafo descreve coisas que ainda nao aconteceram. Avise isso antes, e so isso. Depois UMA frase de resumo.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA. A opcao (a) e a inversao do texto e (c) contradiz o segundo paragrafo -- as duas punem leitura por palavra-chave.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA: TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS a linha que prova. A afirmacao 4 e a mais fina: 'was given but not carried out' x 'was never given'.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: Now the tense the first paragraph is written in. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Nao de a regra. Peca que ela separe os quatro exemplos em ANTES DO PRAZO e NO PRAZO, e depois ache as palavrinhas (by / by the time / by the end of). So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: If the round is completed on arrival, is the order obeyed? (Nao.) A sexta linha da tabela e used to / be used to -- passe por ela rapido, e reconhecimento, nao producao.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Os quatro: futuro simples no lugar do futuro perfeito, 'will have standing', participio sem -ed, e 'is used to work' por 'is used to working'.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same February, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): O quarto par ('Had the fire spread' -> 'If the fire had continued') e a inversao condicional -- callback da aula 5. Peca que ela reconheca sem que voce diga.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a direita e faca a direcao dificil.
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led, uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A ultima (troca de AGENTE: fixed system x crew with portable equipment) e o tipo de distrator que ela ja viu tres vezes -- confira se ela o reconhece sozinha agora.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The engineer who was there, and the manager who wrote the order. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: 0.75x na primeira vez. Pergunte no fim: he says four minutes and a closed door away. What does he mean by that?
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio esta quase todo em futuro perfeito e continuo -- peca que ela conte quantas vezes ouve 'will have' e 'will be'.
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Cinco frases com os frames. Conte quantos futuros perfeitos COM prazo ela produz.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): Proibir 'lucky' e o exercicio: sem a palavra ela tem de descrever o mecanismo (o resultado nao mede a preparacao).
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): Nao interrompa. Mede-se: tres futuros perfeitos, cada um com o proprio 'by', e um futuro continuo.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do proprio texto. Insista na reducao natural: 'will have completed' sai como /wɪləv/ na fala -- e por isso que ela nunca ouviu esse tempo verbal em ingles falado.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 8 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) escrever uma ordem operacional propria de dez linhas para uma chegada em porto, usando pelo menos quatro futuros perfeitos com prazo e dois continuos; (2) ler um resumo de acidente maritimo em ingles e sublinhar tudo que e equipamento de emergencia. Proxima aula: Precision Reading.
